questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The best academic opportunities within Marine Biology

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. I went to the student center, as I knew nothing when I arrived. They were very helpful and got me set up

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
At the student center they helped my with getting my student card, registering my arrival and how to apply for courses. 
Later on, due to their different study calendars (Block, trimester, and semesters). There were different orientations I partook in. They were all good, but at that point (a few weeks into my stay) I already knew most of it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
There were many different options I am only closely familiar with two of them though. 

BY is the newest one located centrally on campus. You have you own room and share bathroom with the entire floor. The kitchen is shared between all residents. 

Rotary is the oldest. is is located at the back of campus towards the mountain. It is therfore sorounded in narture and wildlife. Here you share an apartment with 5 or 6 other residents. You each have you own room. There are two bathrooms and one kitchen you all share. There is also a living room with a TV and two balconies (depending on your block and floor). You have a sink in you room. The rooms are larger than at BY.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
George Roberts offer catering, though I have heard it is not good. 

Otherwise you will have access to a kitchen and be incharge of your own cooking.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
Depending on what accommodation you choose, there is varying levels of social interaction (of course this also varies with who are you floor/roommates). 
At BY you will have more people around you, but there is less of an inbuilt community (due to the large size). 
Rotary allows fewer people around you, and closer contact with those people. It creates an inbuilt community, which is great if you get along, but can be very grating if you don't.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
You have to register to each course timeslot individually. If you already have something in that timeslot you cannot register for it, even if it is mandatory. Then you have to get help at the student center.
The class calendrers are not available until a few weeks prior to start of term. You can only view one calendar at a time, and only one week at a time.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is plenty of help available at the student center

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you start in good time and take all the help you need. Is is an annoyingly complicated process.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I took one 1st year class and three 3rd year classes. I would say the levels matched this. 
All the 3rd year classes were taken together with 1st year master students. The only difference was the master students had a few more assignments and a different final exam.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
All exams are pen and paper. 
The switch to blocks and trimesters is still new and the classes are not set up properly for it.
There is also a plan for all lectures to be turned into 15 minutes online videos with no option for in-person lectures. 
All lectures are recorded, which is nice.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
MB1110 Introductory Marine Science, 3 credit points = 7,5 ECTS 
MB3200 Marine Conservation Biology, 3 credit points = 7,5 ECTS 
MB3190 Coral Reef Ecology, 3 credit points = 7,5 ECTS 
BZ2480 Restoration Ecology, 3 credit points = 7,5 ECTS

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
MB1110 Introductory Marine Science, 3 credit points = 7,5 ECTS 
A good introductory class if you are new to marine sciences. Otherwise, there is a lot of repetition. However, I would still recommend as it provides a nice introduction to JCU as well.

MB3200 Marine Conservation Biology, 3 credit points = 7,5 ECTS 
MB3190 Coral Reef Ecology, 3 credit points = 7,5 ECTS 
Very good classes, thought by leaders in the field. Provides a unique view into the current and historical knowledge in the topics. There is some overlap between the two

BZ2480 Restoration Ecology, 3 credit points = 7,5 ECTS 
Super fun and unique class with tons of independent fieldwork. The class was, however, very unstructured, and you were left on your own for most of it. Next to all lectures were online and hard to follow. Hopefully the structure will improve, as it is very interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to buy your own lab coat and safety goggles if you have any lab work. I also had to buy a calculator for one of my exams as I did not bring one (didn’t think I would need it).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transport is only 1 AUD for a day ticket.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university constantly host all sorts of events. Every Tuesday there was café corner, where you could go get snacks, meet people and play games. There were also larger events held throughout the semester. One included a petting zoo and a climbing wall.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked café corner. If nothing else, it was nice to get some snacks between classes. The larger events were also always fun and often included some free stuff.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Definitely explore as much as you can. The beach may be exiting, but for good swimming experiences visit crystal or alligator creek. Magnetic island has amazing hiking. The snorkelling is not the best dur to high sedimentation. You will get better snorkelling by booking trips out to the proper reef.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I did not experience the culture to be very different, but it definitely depend on what you partake in. I did not really go out to town much. However, I heard that you have to be very careful as there is a lot of crime and people don’t really trust the police.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open to meet new people especially during orientations. You may have to be more persistent later on, as people settle into their groups. The more you participate the easier it is. Roommates and classmates are definitely an easier place to start off.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The fact it was not safe to go out alone, especially after dark.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people I associated with were all very friendly and generous. I was offered rides to the supermarket by multiple people and generally people were good at sharing and helping each other.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be aware that JCU is currently going through lots of changes. The change from semester to blocks and trimesters. The change to online lectures. AND the loss of many excellent professors that previously placed them as one of the best universities for marine science

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Townsville is known in Australia as having lots of criminal activity. People do not trust the police and Queensland in general have a lot more old fashioned people with degrading views of any non Europeans or any one in the LGBTQ+ community. (It is kind of Australia's version of Florida/Texas (not that I have ever been there))

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning about myself. Experiencing Australian wildlife and interacting with it through volunteering. I am also so happy about what I learned of restoration as well as the expanded perspective on marine biology, I learned through my classes.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I ended up enduring a mental health crisis while there, though that was due to a friend I met, not being at James Cook. James Cook University were actually very helpful in that period, as they provided free counselling. Generally, I experienced a much larger focus on metal health while in Australia compared to Denmark.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
